hints.content:
The function $f$ is negative $($i.e. $f(x)<0)$ whenever its graph is below the $x$-axis.

This is because the negative $y$-values are below the $x$-axis, and $y=f(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by one. The graph of the function y equals f of x is above the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative four and three quarters. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative four and three-quarters to x equals negative four. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative four to x equals negative three. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative three to x equals negative two. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative two to x equals two. It is below the x-axis from x equals two to x equals three. It is above the x-axis from x equals three to x equals four. It is below the x-axis from x equals four to x equals four and three-quarters. It is above the x-axis from x equals four and three-quarters to x equals five. The function decreases from x equals negative five to x equals negative four and one-half. The function increases from x equals negative four and one-half to x equals negative three and one-half. The function decreases from x equals negative three and one-half to x equals negative two and one-half. It increases from x equals negative two and one-half to x equals zero. It decreases from x equals zero to x equals two and one-half. It increases from x equals two and one-half to x equals three and one-half. It decreases from x equals three and one-half to x equals four and one-half. It increases from x equals four and one-half to x equals five. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative four and three-quarters to x equals negative four, from x equals negative three to x equals negative two, from x equals two to x equals three, and from x equals four to x equals four and three-quarters.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $-3<x<-2$.
